svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: macOS · Gallery · grid mode, all three panes · 1280×800
svg.desc: Mirrors App/GalleryView.swift (macOS/regular-width branch) + App/GallerySidebar.swift + App/GalleryGridContent.swift (standardGrid) + App/GalleryTile.swift + App/GalleryPreviewPanel.swift, as shipped in 394e48e (2026-09-07). THE THREE-PANE LAYOUT: GalleryView.isWide is hard-coded true on macOS, so the Mac always takes the HStack(spacing: 0) branch — GallerySidebar at a fixed 200pt, hairline Divider, then a VStack of galleryHeader / Divider / GalleryGridContent, and — only while a tile is selected — a second Divider and GalleryPreviewPanel at a fixed 300pt. Both side panels are fixed width, so resizing the window grows the grid alone. WINDOW SIZE, and why this file is drawn at 1280×800 rather than the 760×680 default: galleryHeader is one HStack(spacing: 10) of eight children with no compact form and nothing that collapses — the 32pt sidebar button, the 20pt bold "Gallery" title, a 190pt SceneSearchField, the sort menu + direction button (116pt), the 112pt zoom cluster and the ~89pt Timeline toggle, inside .padding(.horizontal, 16). Its intrinsic width is about 691pt. The centre column is the window minus 201pt of sidebar and 301pt of preview panel, so the header fits only when the WINDOW is about 1193pt wide or more; at the 760×680 default it has 259pt to work in and overflows by roughly 430pt, and with the preview closed it still overflows by about 130pt because gallery.showSidebar defaults to TRUE. In other words the shipped default window cannot draw its own header — see gallery.default-window notes in INDEX.md. 1280×800 is the smallest round size at which the shipped layout renders as designed, and it is what this file specifies; the guided-builder files set the precedent for drawing a Mac screen at the size its layout works at and stating what the default does instead. MEASURED HERE: sidebar 200 (x 20–220); centre column 778 (x 221–999); preview 300 (x 1000–1300). Header band 52pt tall (y 48–100), its children laid out left-to-right at 237 / 313.5-spacer / 323.5 title / 436-spacer / 446 search / 646 sort / 772 zoom / 894 Timeline, ending flush at 983. Grid: .padding(.horizontal, 14) and .padding(.vertical, 14) inside the ScrollView, LazyVGrid of columnCount flexible columns at spacing 12 — at the drawn columnCount of 3 that is a 750pt content width and 242×181.5pt tiles, drawn 4:3 by GalleryTile's .aspectRatio(4/3, contentMode: .fit). Column origins 235 / 489 / 743; row origins 115 / 308.5 / 502 / 695.5. TILE: ProjectThumbnailView at cornerRadius 8; a MediaBadge naming the shoot type pinned bottom-leading with 6pt padding (always shown, black at 50% with white 11.5pt semibold text); an amber MediaBadge reading "N clips" pinned top-trailing with the same padding, drawn only where model.blends(for:).count is 2 or more; and, when selected, a 2.5pt LL.accent strokeBorder on the same 8pt radius. Single click selects (which is what raises the preview panel), double click calls onOpen and pushes ProjectDetailView onto the NavigationStack; right-click raises the context menu (Open · New blended clip · Edit · Show in Finder · Delete…, the Finder entry macOS-only), not drawn. PREVIEW PANEL (300pt, LL.cardBackground, its own ScrollView): 150pt thumbnail at cornerRadius 10 inset 14pt and 22pt from the top (click it to raise ProjectMediaPreviewSheet); title 16pt bold over a 12pt secondary date · size line; a 2×2 LazyVGrid of 132pt action buttons at spacing 8 and cornerRadius 9 — Open is filled LL.accent with white content, Edit / Text / New clip sit on primary at 7%; a full-bleed Divider; five metaRows on a 72pt label column (Tags, In frame, Variations, Storage, Field notes — each rendered only when it has a value, so a freshly imported project shows two); a second full-bleed Divider; and a footer of four equal-width buttons split by 20pt dividers (Rename · Share · Finder · Delete…, Finder macOS-only, Delete tinted red). Tags render through SceneTagLine: up to three LL.accent@13% capsules with LL.accentDeep 10.5pt text, then a secondary "+N". TAB BAR: FloatingTabBar is a sibling of the whole three-pane Group inside ContentView's ZStack(alignment: .bottom), so it floats over sidebar, grid and preview alike, centred on the WINDOW rather than on the grid — 358pt at five 66pt seats, 12pt clear of the bottom edge. BOTTOM CLEARANCE IS DOUBLE-COUNTED, drawn as shipped: ContentView already applies .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { Color.clear.frame(height: 58) } to the tab Group, and all three of the Gallery's scroll views then append their own Color.clear.frame(height: 82) — so the last grid row, the sidebar's Collections row and the preview footer all stop 140pt above the window edge instead of 58pt. TWO MAC-SPECIFIC MISMATCHES ALSO DRAWN AS SHIPPED: the window title reads "Gallery" (GalleryView sets .navigationTitle on the macOS branch, which retitles Window("LetsLapse", id: "main")) while the header repeats the same word 26pt below it; and the zoom Slider is never tinted, so its filled track is system blue and is the one accent-coloured control on the screen that is not LL.accent. STATES NOT DRAWN (desc-only): sidebar collapsed (showSidebar false — the toggle animates the pane out over 0.22s easeInOut and the centre column takes its 201pt, which does NOT fix the header at the default window size); no selection, where the preview panel and its divider are simply absent and the grid takes the 301pt (drawn two-pane in gallery.timeline.svg); the empty state (photo.on.rectangle.angled over "No projects" / "Adjust the filter or search to see your library.", centred in the grid area and shown whenever the filtered set is empty, which on macOS replaces the grid but leaves the header standing); a tag selected in the sidebar, with its "Clear tags" link (drawn in gallery.timeline.svg); the rename alert, the delete confirmationDialog, the export/share sheet and the "Couldn't delete" alert. HOOKS: LL_TAB=gallery brings this tab front; there is no hook for selection, sidebar state, column count or timeline mode — all four are @AppStorage (gallery.showSidebar, gallery.columnCount, gallery.sortKey/sortAscending, gallery.timelineMode) and are set by seeding defaults before launch. NOT YET VERIFIED against the running Mac app: authored from the source in 394e48e on 2026-09-07: measurements here are computed from the Swift layout, not read off a screenshot, and the header-overflow arithmetic in particular is owed a check against a real window. A Release Mac app was running and holds library.json, which has no serialised writer, so a second instance could not be launched safely. **2026-09-07, richer blended-clips list (design-first, code owed):** the preview panel's metaRows lost their one-line "Variations · 3 blended clips" row (Tags, In frame, Storage, Field notes shift up 27pt to close the gap) and gained a full BLENDED CLIPS section at the foot of the panel, below the Rename/Share/Finder/Delete footer (which also shifts up 27pt) — a "BLENDED CLIPS · 3" header over a card of three stacked rows, using the SAME shared component as the iOS project-detail screens (components/blended-clip-row.<state>.narrow.svg — the narrow, 272pt-wide set for this panel's column, versus iOS's 361pt wide set), showing the same three representative rows those screens draw (default, from-codec, true-light) since this demo project's own "3 clips" tile badge and former Variations count agree on three. The window's own #win clip-path trims the bottom ~8pt of the third row — the panel scrolling under the window edge, the same convention the iOS video variant's below-the-fold management card already draws. This was Part 1 of a two-part pass (LetsLapse/docs/design components refactor). **2026-09-07, Part 2 (design-first, this same day, tick-chip revision later the same day):** the filter now sits between the header and the list — components/blend-list-filter.<state>.narrow.svg, four independent tick chips (Blends, Slices, Image, Video, all ticked here) wrapping to two rows at this width — pushing the card down 83pt and clipping more of the third row against the window edge (see the blended-clips-list comment just above). An earlier two-facet segmented-control draft was replaced same-day (Steven: ticking all four already means "All", so no separate All segment is needed — see components/README.md). Neither Part is wired to real filtering in App/GalleryPreviewPanel.swift yet.
svg.text: macOS · Gallery · grid mode, sidebar + preview · 1280×800 pt window
mirrors App/GalleryView.swift + GallerySidebar + GalleryGridContent + GalleryTile + GalleryPreviewPanel — the 760×680 default window cannot draw this header (see desc)
